issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal and its concrete subclasses: the problem statement UML and the template Main show/expect single-argument constructors that accept only a name (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle") in the commented Main), while the solution implementation declares constructors that require two parameters (String name, int age) for Animal and for Seal/Pig/Goat. This discrepancy will cause code that follows the template Main or the UML to fail to compile against the solution API and will confuse students about the expected constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor signatures consistent across artifacts. Option A: change the solution to provide single-argument constructors (String name) for Animal and its subclasses (and remove or make age optional), and update solution constructors accordingly (also adjust any uses). Option B: update the problem statement UML and the template Main to require two-argument constructors (String name, int age) and update the example code in Main to construct animals with both arguments. Apply the chosen approach consistently to problem_statement.md, the template Main, and the solution code so students can compile and run the example code without signature errors.

issues.description: Attribute mismatch for class Animal: the problem statement UML specifies a single attribute name: String on Animal, but the solution's Animal class declares an additional attribute age: int (in addition to name). This adds an unexpected field that is not described in the exercise specification, and it is the likely reason the solution constructors require an extra parameter. Students may be confused about whether they must implement the age attribute and related getters/setters.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Animal attributes with the problem specification. Option A: remove the age attribute from the solution (keep only name) and provide matching single-argument constructors and getters/setters. Option B: update the problem statement and UML to include age: int (and update examples in the template Main), and document that students should implement the age attribute and corresponding constructor parameter. Ensure whichever option is chosen is applied consistently across problem_statement.md, the template, and the reference solution.
